metadata.source: Digital Corpus of Sanskrit (DCS), text ID 182. http://www.sanskrit-linguistics.org/dcs/ Segmentation follows the DCS line/pāda boundaries; chapter and verse labels are taken from the DCS references.

children.translated_text: For the earth: bhūḥ, bhūtadhātrī, girikarṇikā, abdhidvīpā, samudrāmbaramekhalā, and kuḥ.

children.text: kṣamādrikīlā ca jagadvahā ca puṃsi smṛtau madhyamalokamartyau ||
children.translated_text: Also kṣamā, adrikīlā, and jagadvahā; in the masculine, smṛti, madhyamaloka, and martya.

children.text: sahā kāntā gandhavatī ratnagarbhā ca medinī
children.translated_text: Also sahā, kāntā, gandhavatī, ratnagarbhā, and medinī.

children.text: svasthalī bhāratākhyaṃ tu varṣaṃ haimavataṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: They know the land called <s>Bhārata</s> as svasthalī and haimavata.
<s>Bhārata</s>, narabhūḥ, kiṃpūruṣa, then harivarṣa,
bhadrāśva, uttarakuru, hiraṇmaya, and ilāvṛta:
these are the nine varṣas of the earth, and likewise
the seven islands are <s>Jambū</s>, <s>Plakṣa</s>, <s>Kuśa</s>, <s>Krauñca</s>, <s>Śāka</s>, <s>Śālmali</s>, and <s>Puṣkara</s>.

children.text: dvīpāḥ saptātha saptaiva samudrā api kīrtitāḥ
children.translated_text: And the seven oceans too are declared to be
made of salt, sugarcane juice, liquor, ghee, curds, milk, and water.
Uṣara, tūṣavān, ūṣa, brahmāvarta, and tapovaṭa:
between <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, <s>Prayāga</s>, the <s>Himādri</s>, and the <s>Vindhya</s>
is the Madhyadeśa. Then the Puṇḍras are the Varendrī and the Gauḍa country.
<s>Prabhāsa</s> is Somatīrtha, and Antarvedī is Kuśasthalī.
Prāgjyotiṣa is in <s>Kāmarūpa</s>; Tīrabhukti is Nicchavi.
The Videhas; and in <s>Kaśmīra</s> the Kīras are skilled in sciences and crafts.
The Turuṣkas, Khaśas, Yaṣṭakkas, Vāhlīkas, and Trigartakas,
the Daśerakas, desert peoples, Mālavas, and Avantayas.
The Ḍāhalas and Cedis are Caidyas; the Kārūṣas are Bṛhadgṛhas.

children.text: yadavastu daśārhāḥ syuḥ sātvatāḥ kukurāśca te ||
children.translated_text: The Yadavas are the Daśārhas; they are also Sātvatas and Kukuras.
The Oṇḍras are called Utkalas; the Magadhas are considered Kīkaṭas.
Velākūla, Tāmalipta, Tāmaliptī, and Tamālikā.
Ekacakra, Harigṛha, Śaṃbhupurī, and then Vartani.
The eastern country; then <s>Sāketa</s>, <s>Ayodhyā</s>, and Uttarakośalā.
Kuśasthala, Kānyakubja, Nāgāṅga, and Hastināpura;
Gajāhva and Hāstina; then Śrāvastī is Dharmapattana.
Kurukṣetra is Vinaśana; Kauśāmbī is Vatsapattana.
Prayāga is Prājāpatya; Dvārakā is Vanamālinī.
Dvāravatī and Abdhinagarī are the same; Videhā and Mithilā are the same.

children.text: mathurā tu madhūpaghnaṃ jitvarī tu tapaḥsthalī ||
children.translated_text: Mathurā is Madhūpaghna; Jitvarī is Tapaḥsthalī.
Vārāṇasī is Tīrtharājī; Viśālā and Ujjayinī are the same.
Campā is Mālinī; Puṣpapura is Pāṭaliputraka.
Devīkoṭa, Bāṇapura, Koṭīvarṣa, and Umāvana;
Śoṇitapura; then yojana is Mārgadhenuka.
Krimiśaila is Valmīka; Śakramūrdhan, and then Saṃcara.

children.text: dharaṇaḥ piṇḍalaḥ setuḥ panthāstu kṣullamo vahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Dharaṇa, Piṇḍala, Setu; a road is kṣullama and vaha.

children.text: vāṭaḥ pathaśca māthaśca khapuraṃ tūrdhvagaṃ puram
children.translated_text: Vāṭa, patha, and mātha; Khapura is the upper city.
Hariścandrapura, Śaubha, Udraṅga, and Pratimārgaka.
Traṅga and atraṅga; nirmuṭa refers to Paṇyājīvaka-caṅgala.

children.text: puṃsi haṭṭakrayārohau janyaṃ grāmamukhaṃ ca tat ||
children.translated_text: In the masculine, haṭṭa, kraya, and āroha; that is also janya and grāmamukha.
It may also be called abhiṣyandi-vamana and śākhānagara.
Śāsana is dharmakīla; makuti is a Śūdra settlement.
Paṭṭolikā, the corruptly transmitted kﾱptakīlā, and pāṃsukīla belong to no one in particular.
An aṅguṣṭha is made of six yavas; with twelve of these
there is a vitasti; from two of those there is a hasta, and four of that
make a daṇḍa or dhanvantara; by two thousand of it
there is a krośa; by two of those a gavyūti, and twice that is considered a yojana.
Within a hundred and forty-eight villages are the droṇamukha and karvaṭa.
In a house, garbhāgāra and apavaraka are inner rooms; vāstu is the house-site or house itself.
Prāsāda is devakula; putrikā is śālabhañjikā.

children.text: oko gṛhaṃ piṭaṃ cālo valabhī candraśālikā
children.translated_text: Oka, gṛha, piṭa, cāla, valabhī, and candraśālikā are house terms.
Kūṭāgāra; then kapiśīrṣa and ghoṭakaśīrṣaka.
Kramaśīrṣa; then kharakuṭī and nāpitaśālikā.
Kuśālikā, pakṣiśālā, kārāveśma, and vadhāṅgaka.
Kāyamāna, tṛṇakuṭī, darbhaṭa, and a secluded house.
Kuḍaṅga, udghāṭa, and piṭhara; indrakoṣa is a small bed or couch.
Vāsāgāra and bhogagṛha; kanyā, patnī, āṭani, and niṣkuṭa are women's apartments or inner quarters.
Devīgṛha is valabhī; layana is a Buddhist residence.
In Śiva's bull-pavilion, the learned remember the term gopiṭaka.
Vātāyana is gavākṣa; and vadhūṭaśayana likewise.
Upaśalya and upakaṇṭha are two terms for vicinity; kapāṭa is dvārakaṇṭaka.
Kavāṭa, cārara, kanthāvāṭa, and prākāra are also said.

children.text: śaile sthāvaradhātubhṛddharakukīlo vyaṃśakaḥ sānumāñjīmūtaḥ pṛthuśekharaśca kaṭakī dantī nago nirjharī
children.translated_text: For a mountain: śaila, sthāvaradhātubhṛt, dharakukīla, vyaṃśaka, sānumat, jīmūta, pṛthuśekhara, kaṭakī, dantī, naga, and nirjharī.

children.text: kuṭṭāro'tha himālayo nagapatirmenādhavomāgurū kailāse gaṇaparvataśca rajataprasthaḥ kuberācalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Also kuṭṭāra; then <s>Himālaya</s> is Nagapati, Menādhava, and Umāguru; on <s>Kailāsa</s> are Gaṇaparvata, Rajataprastha, and Kuberācala.
Hiraṇyanābha, Maināka, and Sunābha are sons of <s>Himavat</s>.

children.text: śailāgre śikharaṃ śṛṅgaṃ dantaḥ prāgbhāra ityapi ||
children.translated_text: For a mountain-top: śikhara, śṛṅga, danta, and prāgbhāra.
The eastern mountain is Dinamūrdhan; the western mountain is Caramācala.
The sandal mountain is Malaya; Kauñca, Krauñca, and Mālyavān.
Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Śuktimān, and Pāriyātraka,
Ṛkṣa and Vindhya: these seven are the family mountains of Jambūdvīpa.
For stone: aśman, pajharuka, pāṭa, pāraṭīṭa, and mṛnmaru.
Gharṣaṇāla, śilāputra, gṛhāśman, and gṛhakacchapa.
Gairika is vanālakta, raktadhātu, and gaveruka.
Pratyaśman and girimṛd; and śilādhātu is sitopala.

children.text: mṛtkolo varṇalekhā ca kaṭhinī kakkhaṭī khaṭī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mṛtkola</s>, <s>varṇalekhā</s>, <s>kaṭhinī</s>, <s>kakkhaṭī</s>, and <s>khaṭī</s> are synonymous names.

children.text: vārkṣaṃ vanaṃ talaṃ talkaṃ hiṅgulaṃ samajaṃ trasam
children.translated_text: <s>Vārkṣa</s>, <s>vana</s>, <s>tala</s>, <s>talka</s>, <s>hiṅgula</s>, <s>samaja</s>, and <s>trasa</s> are listed as names connected with woodland or trees.

children.text: līlodyānaṃ devanaṃ syād riñcholī paṅktir āvalī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Līlodyāna</s> and <s>devana</s> mean a pleasure garden; <s>riñcholī</s>, <s>paṅkti</s>, and <s>āvalī</s> mean a row or series.

children.text: vṛkṣaḥ kāraskaro gacchaḥ palāśī viṣṭaraḥ sthiraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛkṣa</s>, <s>kāraskara</s>, <s>gaccha</s>, <s>palāśī</s>, <s>viṣṭara</s>, and <s>sthira</s> are names for a tree.
<s>Caitya</s> means a sacred tree or shrine-tree; in a divine dwelling the terms <s>kari-bha</s> and <s>kuñjara</s> are also given.
A shade-tree is <s>chāyātaru</s> or <s>sthiracchāya</s>; <s>vandā</s> is remembered as <s>kākaruhā</s>.
<s>Vanaspatī</s> is <s>nirluṭa</s>; <s>phulla</s>, <s>unnidra</s>, and <s>vikasvara</s> mean blossoming or opened.
<s>Smita</s> and <s>unmudra</s> also mean opened; <s>kiliñja</s> is fine wood, and then <s>pallava</s> means a sprout.
<s>Bisala</s> and <s>kisala</s> mean a young shoot; <s>utkalikā</s> and <s>aṅgārita</s> are equivalent.

children.text: guccho guluñchaḥ kṣepaḥ syāccamarī mañjaraṃ na nā
children.translated_text: <s>Guccha</s>, <s>guluñcha</s>, and <s>kṣepa</s> mean a cluster; <s>camarī</s> and <s>mañjara</s> are not neuter.

children.text: mañjiśca gondī gundī ca makarando marandavat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mañjī</s>, <s>gondī</s>, and <s>gundī</s> are names; <s>makaranda</s> is also called <s>marandavat</s>.
<s>Vedhaka</s> means a thorn; <s>pattrasūcī</s>, <s>drunakha</s>, and <s>vaṅkilā</s> are likewise thorn-names.
<s>Pippala</s> is <s>vādaraṅga</s>; the sacred fig is <s>caityadru</s> and <s>keśavālaya</s>.
<s>Yakṣodumbaraka</s> denotes its fruit; next, <s>gṛhanāśana</s> is a name.
<s>Devavṛkṣa</s>, <s>dānagandhi</s>, <s>saptapattra</s>, and <s>śirorujā</s> are names of the same plant.
<s>Dantaharṣaṇa</s> and <s>jambīra</s> are names; <s>kataka</s> is the water-clearing plant.
<s>Varuṇa</s> is the stone-destroyer; then <s>madhudruma</s> is enjoyable for travellers.
<s>Kapicūta</s> denotes <s>amrātaka</s>; its fruit is called <s>paśuharītakī</s>.
<s>Pikabandhu</s> is the mango; it is <s>strīpriya</s>, beloved by women, and <s>ṣaṭpadātithi</s>, host to bees.
<s>Madhudūta</s> and <s>vasantadru</s> are names for the mango; <s>mahākāla</s> and <s>urukālaka</s> are also listed.
<s>Śobhāñjana</s> is called <s>strīcittahārī</s>, stealer of women's hearts, and <s>vidradhināśana</s>, destroyer of abscesses.
It is also <s>prābhāñjana</s>; next, <s>prācīnapanasa</s> is <s>goharītakī</s>.
<s>Mahākapittha</s> and <s>bilva</s> are names; <s>kolī</s> is remembered as <s>gṛdhranakhī</s>.
It is <s>picchiladalā</s>, with slimy leaves, and <s>svāduphalā</s>, sweet-fruited; then <s>nagaraṅgaka</s> is named.
<s>Takrādhivāsī</s> and <s>nāraṅga</s> are names; <s>kirmīra</s> is <s>tvaksugandhaka</s>, fragrant-barked.
<s>Dharmaṇa</s> is <s>picchilatvak</s>, slimy-barked; <s>dhava</s> is <s>madhuratvaca</s>, sweet-barked.
<s>Piśācadru</s>, <s>pītaphala</s>, <s>śākhoṭa</s>, and <s>karkaśacchada</s> are names of a rough-leaved yellow-fruited tree.
<s>Arśohita</s>, useful against piles, and <s>rakṣoghna</s>, demon-destroying, are names of <s>bhallātakī</s>; next comes <s>śālmalī</s>.
<s>Śālmalī</s> is remembered as <s>durārohā</s>; <s>piṇḍītagara</s> is phlegm-increasing.
<s>Kākaciñcī</s> is <s>tulābīja</s>; <s>khadira</s> is <s>bālapattraka</s>.
<s>Khadira</s> is the sacrificial-post tree and remover of skin disease; next, <s>karañja</s> is <s>ghṛtapūrṇaka</s>.
<s>Rasāyanaphalā</s>, <s>pathyā</s>, <s>śakasṛṣṭā</s>, and <s>sudhodbhavā</s> are names of the wholesome fruit.
<s>Sarala</s> is the incense tree; <s>śoṇaka</s> is <s>nyaṅkubhūruha</s>.
<s>Campakālu</s> has drum-like fruit; that is also <s>panasa</s>, the jackfruit.
<s>Ḍahu</s> is the small sour jackfruit; <s>nicula</s> has red clusters.
<s>Nimba</s> is <s>arkapādapa</s>; <s>puṇyagandha</s> is <s>kusumādhirāṭ</s>, king of flowers.
<s>Campaka</s> is <s>varalabdha</s>; <s>vakula</s> is <s>siṃhakesara</s>.
<s>Vakula</s> is <s>śīdhugandha</s>; then <s>kaṅkelli</s> and <s>naṭa</s> are names, and <s>kāntāṅghridohada</s> is the tree that longs for a beloved woman's foot.
<s>Aśoka</s> is <s>piṇḍapuṣpa</s>; <s>dāḍima</s> is <s>phalaśāḍava</s>.

children.text: dāḍimbaḥ parvaruṭ ca syāt svādvamblaḥ śukavallabhaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Dāḍimba</s> is also <s>parvaruṭ</s>, <s>svādvambla</s>, and <s>śukavallabha</s>, beloved of parrots.
<s>Piṇḍīra</s>; then <s>suvarṇebhanāga</s> is the tree called <s>nāgakesara</s>.
It is also <s>puṣparocana</s>; its powder is <s>haridrava</s>.
<s>Niśipuṣpā</s> is <s>śephālī</s>; <s>kuṭaja</s> is <s>pāṇḍuradruma</s>, the pale tree.
<s>Latāśaṅkutaru</s> is <s>śāla</s>; <s>nīpa</s> is <s>dhārākadambaka</s>.
<s>Kaṭaṃkaṭerī</s> is <s>haridrā</s>; <s>śiṃśapā</s> is <s>yugmapattrikā</s>, the paired-leaved tree.

children.text: paṭolaṃ syādrājaphalaṃ tasya mūle tu ramyakam
children.translated_text: <s>Paṭola</s> is <s>rājaphala</s>; at its root is <s>ramyaka</s>.
<s>Sūtrapuṣpa</s> denotes cotton; <s>jīrṇaparṇa</s> is <s>kadambaka</s>.

children.text: prahasantī tu yūthī syād damanaḥ puṣpacāmaraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Prahasantī</s> is <s>yūthī</s>; <s>damana</s> is <s>puṣpacāmara</s>.
The flower-bud of <s>mālatī</s> is known as <s>saumanasyāyanī</s>.

children.text: kunde syād voraṭaḥ puṃsi graiṣmī tu navamālikā
children.translated_text: For <s>kunda</s>, the masculine word is <s>voraṭa</s>; <s>graiṣmī</s> is <s>navamālikā</s>.
<s>Raktapiṇḍa</s> is <s>oṇḍrapuṣpa</s>; <s>amlāna</s> is <s>kuraṇṭaka</s>.
<s>Kandala</s> and <s>śilīndhrapuṣpa</s> are names; <s>tripuramallikā</s> is said to remove phlegm.
<s>Eraṇḍa</s> is <s>hastikarṇa</s>; <s>prācīnāmalaka</s> and <s>vāribadara</s> are two names.
<s>Bṛhatpāṭali</s> and <s>dhustūra</s> are names; <s>kadalī</s> is <s>āyatacchadā</s>, long-leaved.
<s>Kadalī</s> is <s>tantuvigrahā</s>, <s>mañjiphalā</s>, and <s>vāraṇavallabhā</s>, beloved of elephants.
<s>Vātiṅgaṇa</s>, <s>vārtāku</s>, <s>vārtāka</s>, and <s>śākabilvaka</s> are names for eggplant.
In the neuter it is <s>vaṅga</s>; the feminine is <s>vārtākī</s>, and it is also called <s>mahābṛhatī</s>.
<s>Kuṣṭha</s>, <s>gadāhvaya</s>, and <s>mūla</s> are names; its root is <s>puṣkaramūlaka</s>.
<s>Vaṅgasena</s> is <s>agastidru</s>; <s>śukanāsa</s> is <s>munidruma</s>.
<s>Anali</s> and <s>kunalī</s> are names; <s>putraṃjīva</s> removes elephantiasis.
<s>Chattraka</s> is <s>mallipattra</s>; <s>kubjaka</s> is <s>vajrakaṇṭaka</s>.
<s>Vāstūka</s>, <s>ṣaṭkadeśīya</s>, <s>śākavīra</s>, and <s>ghanāmala</s> are names.
<s>Śothajit</s>, conqueror of swelling, <s>garahā</s>, and <s>kālaśāka</s> are also names; next is <s>mahauṣadhī</s>.
<s>Mahī</s>, <s>viṣaghnī</s>, <s>cakrāṅgī</s>, <s>matsyākṣī</s>, and <s>hilamocikā</s> are names.
<s>Jalabrahmī</s> and <s>sālīñca</s> are names; <s>pakūra</s> is <s>lohamāraka</s>, destroyer of iron.
<s>Kecuka</s>, <s>peculī</s>, <s>pecā</s>, <s>nārīca</s>, and <s>viśvalocana</s> are names.
<s>Keśarāja</s>, <s>nāgamāra</s>, <s>pararu</s>, and <s>bhaṅgasodara</s> are names.
<s>Suniṣaṇṇa</s> and masculine <s>cacu</s> are names; <s>chattrapattra</s> is <s>tamālaka</s>.
Then <s>sthalapadma</s> is known as <s>devapatnī</s> and <s>madhvāluka</s>.

children.text: phalapuccho varaṇḍāluḥ syād raṅgeṣṭālukaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: <s>Phalapuccha</s> is <s>varaṇḍālu</s>; whatever is <s>raṅgeṣṭāluka</s> is also so called.
<s>Śrīmastaka</s> and <s>svastika</s> are names; <s>rāhūcchiṣṭa</s> is <s>rasonaka</s>, garlic.
<s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> is <s>ghṛṇāvāsa</s>; <s>timiṣa</s> is the village cucumber.
<s>Vālukī</s>, <s>karkaṭī</s>, <s>vāru</s>, <s>mūtralā</s>, and <s>romaśā</s> are its names.
<s>Celāna</s>, <s>citraphala</s>, <s>sukhāśa</s>, and <s>rājatāmiṣa</s> are names.
<s>Latāpanasa</s> and <s>āṭāmra</s> are names; the one called <s>seṭu</s> is <s>ūrdhvāsita</s>.
<s>Parāka</s> and <s>kāravella</s> denote that same plant; <s>goḍumbā</s> and <s>gajacirbhiṭa</s> are also names.
<s>Mṛtyubīja</s> is <s>vaṃśa</s>; <s>ketaka</s> is <s>krakacacchada</s>.
<s>Dṛkkaṭa</s> is <s>bahumūla</s>; in the case of <s>karīra</s>, there is <s>veṇukarkaṭa</s>.
<s>Kāśa</s> is <s>aśvavāla</s>, <s>kākekṣu</s>, <s>vanahāsa</s>, and <s>cūrṇalā</s>.
<s>Guḍadāru</s> is <s>madhutṛṇa</s>; <s>ikṣu</s> is <s>asipattraka</s>.
<s>Khānodaka</s>, <s>nālikera</s>, <s>karakāmbhas</s>, and <s>śiraḥphala</s> are synonyms.
<s>Surañjana</s>, <s>gopadala</s>, <s>rājatāla</s>, and <s>chaṭāphala</s> are synonyms.
<s>Karamaṭṭa</s>, <s>tantusāra</s>, <s>guvāka</s>, and also <s>jhora</s> are synonyms.
<s>Rāmapūga</s>, <s>kāmīna</s>, <s>munipūga</s>, and <s>sarevaṭa</s> are synonyms for areca.
<s>Pūgaroṭa</s> is <s>hintāla</s>; <s>tiriṭi</s> is neuter and denotes its fruit.

children.text: ghanāmayaḥ syāt kharjūro dvau tu kācimabhañjarū
children.translated_text: <s>Ghanāmaya</s> is <s>kharjūra</s>; the two trees <s>kācima</s> and <s>bhañjaru</s> are mentioned.
For a tree born in a temple precinct, <s>devakulodbhūta</s> is used; <s>dūrvā</s> is <s>haritālikā</s>.
